survivors.reason: A larger ViewLength (24) only adds room nothing uses. Each view holds 23 bytes at most. The runs view: one byte, two one-byte white-space runs and two digit runs of at most ten digits, since Value caps at Beyond. The lead: one byte and two numbers of at most ten digits, each followed by a space. Every write lands below index 23, every TryFormat that fits 23 bytes fits more, and nothing reads _runs.Length or _lead.Length. So the extra room is never written or read.

With ViewLength 22, the runs view drops a ten-digit number that comes after another ten-digit run, so the header is taken at the earlier run (102 instead of 113). The lead overruns its 22 bytes on its trailing space and throws IndexOutOfRangeException.

Same reason as HT-0003 (ViewLength 34): no view holds more than 23 bytes, all writes and successful TryFormat calls stay below that, and no code reads a view's length, so the extra room is never touched.

Same reason as HT-0003 (ViewLength 25): no view holds more than 23 bytes, all writes and successful TryFormat calls stay below that, and no code reads a view's length, so the extra room is never touched.

With ViewLength 21, TryFormat fails on the second ten-digit run, which is dropped. In the runs view the header comes out at 102 instead of 113. In the lead, the header number is dropped and the header is taken at the run before it (100 instead of 111).

A view's first byte is never an end of line. A lead's first byte is ' ' or 'x'. A runs view's first byte is either a read byte after the read's last end of line or a carried byte (' ', a digit, or an earlier first byte). So crossing that byte as white space leaves endOfLine unchanged, lineEnd is 0 from either index, and nothing before the byte is read: the walk returns the same numbers. The harness's unconfirmed failure is not a kill: CorpusReadingTests.Damaged_documents_are_recovered_as_far_as_an_independent_tool_recovers_them passed three times alone with this mutant applied (129/0/129 each). The harness's one failure was the test's 20 s guard on validation time (28 s under load), not a wrong result.

In the lead view the walk starts at -1 and only moves down, reading lead bytes alone (' ', 'x' and digits, written only by CarryLead and the constructor). So endOfLine is never true in that view, and the `view == View.Runs` test changes nothing.

Whenever a lead holds more than its first byte, its byte at -1 is a space (CarryLead always ends with one), and a space is white space but not an end of line. Starting the walk at -2 therefore puts it where it would stand after crossing that space, with endOfLine still false. A lead of its first byte alone returns the numbers from either index. The harness's unconfirmed failure is not a kill: the damaged-documents theory passed three times alone with this mutant applied (129/0/129 each), and the harness's one failure was the same validation-time guard (28 s against 20 s under load).

Only a runs view's first byte can be a digit, since a lead's is ' ' or 'x'. When it is, the view is 'digit, space, digits, space, digits': its fourth run is white space, or it inherits the first byte from a view of that shape. A walk always enters a view at its last byte from the read. It then takes both digit runs (count reaches 2) and stops at the space before them, so the digit loop never reads the first byte. Without the bound the loop therefore never steps past it.

Same reason as HT-0239: a first byte that is a digit occurs only in a runs view shaped 'digit, space, digits, space, digits', and a walk entering that view takes both digit runs and stops at the space, so the digit loop never tests the first byte and `>=` never gets the chance to take it. The harness's unconfirmed failure is not a kill: the damaged-documents theory passed three times alone with this mutant applied (129/0/129 each), and the harness's one failure was the validation-time guard (28 s against 20 s under load).
